coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Ley 5407/15 and Ley 6368/19 make households register domestic workers with IPS (insurance on minimum wage; part-time from 16 h/week). Only about 7% of roughly 235,000 workers insured (2019-2022). IPS/MTESS formalization campaigns exist. Pain is real but IPS filing is simple; K10/K12 cover payroll. One weak candidate logged.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Ley 294 EIA and municipal licensing (tinglado of at least G. 100M plus EIA of about G. 16M) are impossible for small scrapyards; Asociación Paraguay Recicla protested in Aug 2024 and a MADES/DNIT dialogue table was planned. No scrap register or record-keeping duty found. Nothing new beyond K05.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Casas de empeño are SEPRELAD obligated subjects (Res 375/2016); SIRO access and ROS/RN filing mandated by a Feb-Mar 2023 resolution (Ferrere). No rule found for general second-hand dealers. Logged as the SIRO candidate.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: SEPRELAD Res 222/20: jewellery, stone and precious-metal dealers must register or re-register in SIRO (from 19 Sep 2022, all by 1 Jan 2023) and have a compliance officer and risk manual. Periodic report content and thresholds not confirmed.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Ley 2716/05 as amended by Ley 3369/07: dismantling needs a DISA non-stolen report and a Certificado de Baja y Desarme, and parts invoices must carry the identifier matching the certificate. It also applies to anyone who stores or transports used parts. Current enforcement and any DISA digital system not verified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: SIGOR establishment codes and GOTA transit certificates for every cattle movement (SENACSA). Ranch side is K02. Trader, fair and haulier duties not confirmed.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: SENACSA counts 79 slaughterhouses and says approval also needs sanitary and environmental permits from other bodies (slow). No butcher-level register found. The Decreto 333 hit was a Panama source, so it was discarded.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Only an old 1977 beekeeping law and about 1,000 t of honey per year. No beekeeper register or traceability duty found. Nothing.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Ley 2426/04 and Decreto 649/05 give SENACSA's Registro y Control de Productos Veterinarios authority over veterinary product establishments. Regente and record-book duties not confirmed. Unverified lead.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Drillers must register (Res SEAM 2155/05 and 2273/06, validity to be checked); Ley 3239/07 and the Registro Nacional de Recursos Hídricos (Res SEAM 2194/07); MADES found 10 unlicensed boreholes in Boquerón in Oct 2025. Municipalities ask for a geologist regente.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Ley 5428/15 on effluents. A 2011 Contraloría audit found cesspool trucking unregulated and dumping clandestinely. No current MADES haulier register confirmed.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No national lift or boiler inspection law found. Responsibility sits with the owner, and building approval follows Asunción's 1990 ordinance. Post-fire scrutiny of building inspections in May and July 2026 could produce new rules. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: 2,500-3,500 Juntas de Saneamiento serve about 45% of the population. 90% have under 200 connections, none hold a concession and their tariffs are not ERSSAN-approved (World Bank, via Última Hora 2020). They fall under the Ley 6446 annual register. Related to K04.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Decreto 2048/04 requires registration of aerial applicators and application records. Ley 123/91 and Ley 3742/09 apply. Dealer registration and agronomic prescription rules not found. Nothing new beyond K06.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No Paraguayan agency licensing law or register found. Only the MTESS EmpleaPy portal and the REOP employer register. Nothing.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only the municipal cemetery tax (Ley 620/76, amended by Ley 135/91, permits for burial and transfer). No funeral or private cemetery register found. Nothing.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Ley 6446/2019 and Res 8/2022: annual register update by 30 June, fines of 50-500 jornales. SEPRELAD Res 490/2022 makes OSFL obligated subjects. A 2024 Senate bill on OSFL control and transparency, with unknown status. Halal and kosher are not applicable (no market found). One candidate logged.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi licensing is municipal (for example 286 licensed taxis in Encarnación) and the sector is in conflict with ride apps. Decreto 5.702/2026 changes vehicle registry fees from 1 May 2026. No recurring report duty found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Law 2794/05: cambistas need a BCP registration (annual) and report semi-annually, but only 11-15 are registered against about 1,000 informal (ABC 2025). They are not SEPRELAD obligated subjects. Asunción street-vending permits via the municipal police, and a 2025 Senate bill for a national vendor register. Weak.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries (EDI) need MEC habilitación plus a municipal patente; enforcement is reactive after a 2024 death. DINAVISA Res 326/2025 and 328/2025 require a Registro de Establecimiento and RSPA for processed foods, and INAN's functions moved to DINAVISA. Nothing found on tattoo studios, driving schools or hunting outfitters.

candidates.name: AML compliance kit for used-car lots and vehicle importers/consignors (Res 196/2020: manual, compliance officer, KYC, ROS, negative reports, annual evaluation, external audit)
candidates.trigger: SEPRELAD Res 196 of 4 Sept 2020 (Ferrere). Obligations: AML/CFT manual and code of ethics; compliance officer (the owner may fill it in a sole proprietorship); KYC with a simplified route up to 15 minimum wages; ROS; negative report if no ROS in 3 months; risk assessment every 2 years; annual evaluation reported to SEPRELAD within 90 days of fiscal year end; external audit report within 180 days. coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security is regulated by Ley 5424/15; the Policia Nacional (Departamento de Control y Fiscalizacion de Empresas de Seguridad, under Delitos Economicos) licenses agencies and issues guard credentials (reglamento: Resolucion Policia N 2 of 4 Jan 2016). Licensed counts conflict across sources and are dated: 352 registered with about 100 removed for inactivity, about 252 authorised (La Nacion, Oct 2022); 135 registered (La Nacion, Jun 2023); roughly 300 more operate unregistered. About 60,000 guards (union figure, 2023). A Senate working group is amending Ley 5424 (Ultima Hora; the page is dated 2023 although its header shows later, and a separate Ultima Hora listing is dated 21 Jul 2026; bill text not found). Electronic-security installers have a separate personal licence. Armoured cash-transport fleets need annual verification (art. 50, per a DNCP tender query). In Jul 2026 the Labour Minister (Recalde) met IPS and DNCP about cleaning and guard outsourcers: many complaints, some already sanctioned by MTESS, and a planned bill so sanctioned firms cannot bid again. DNCP contract administrators are to be trained in labour law. The public-procurement bill in the Senate (Jul 2026) would lengthen supplier bans from 3 to 5 years. IPS Res. C.A. 016-006/2026 lets IPS register workers and employers ex officio after MTESS inspections. No dedicated MTESS registry of outsourcing firms found. Capital, bond and renewal requirements not found (unverified). Local guard-control software: none found; DNCP tenders sometimes require a Sistema de Control de Guardias. Only generic foreign products (C-Guard Pro, Guard Patrol, ShiftFlow).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Quarries: MOPC Viceministerio de Minas y Energia runs a Catastro de Canteras Web (about 151 licensed stone and lime quarries, article dated 23 Jan 2025). Permits needed: prior MADES environmental licence, municipal patente and Digemabel/Dimabel authorisation to buy explosives. Digemabel makes quarries file a plan de fuego, get approval, then declare use of each coded unit in its system (SID). After the Jun 2026 Santa Rita bank robbery, which used explosives declared as used at a quarry in Emboscada, Digemabel Res. 260/2026 (18 Jun 2026) set extraordinary controls: mandatory in-person oversight of each blast in Ita, Emboscada and San Lazaro, purchase restrictions, and scrutiny of declared-versus-actual use. Operators pay part of the fiscalisation cost (fuel and some military staff). The Senate (Jul 2026) is working on easing legal purchase while keeping control. Imports of explosives exceed 2,000,000 kg per year (2024), 98% going to quarrying, worth about G. 100,000 million. Intermediaries must register under Dimabel Res. 244/22. MADES environmental audit reports follow SEAM Res. 201/2015 and must be signed by a consultant in the CTCA register (Decreto 954/13); a general audit period for quarries or builders was not found. No MOPC contractor registry or category scheme found; the only contractor list is the DNCP supplier registry (SICP/IDAP), and CAPACO is a trade body. No Paraguay-specific construction-site safety rule from 2025-2026 found. General labour rules apply to builders: digital Libros de Informacion Laboral (MTESS Res. 462/2026, extension Res. 805/2026) and MIPYME contract registration (Res. 220/2026 under Ley 7444/2025). Sand and river-dredging permit rules not found (unverified).
